A1.justification: Both PDFs describe V2V3D, and all 11 pages of each support reliable comparison of text, equations, figures, tables, and references. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix; both refer to separate supplementary materials.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original synthetic and real-data reconstruction experiments, efficiency measurements, macro-scene evaluation, and component ablations.

after.justification: Section 4 retains these original experimental results, including the quantitative comparisons in Tables 1–3 and qualitative results in Figures 4–7.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same two-branch view-to-view framework, PSF-based feature alignment, network architecture, volume averaging, and three loss terms. The IBRNet adaptation in Section 4.4 is also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same six biological categories for synthetic LFM evaluation, real mouse brain and neutrophil measurements, and noisy views of the LLFF Fern scene.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain RLD, VCDNet, DINER, DeepCAD+RLD, and DeepCAD+DINER. Figure 7 retains the same pretrained and fine-tuned IBRNet comparators.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1–4.4 retain the 1,618-volume dataset, 11 test cases, 100-frame real-data sequences, background subtraction before PSNR/SSIM evaluation, and the same Fern subsampling and Gaussian-noise settings.

E4.justification: Table 3 retains the same ablations of view-to-view training, feature alignment, FFT loss, and de-crosstalk loss. The noisy macro-scene validation and discussion of alternative fusion strategies are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same per-scene scores and averages. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and the result figures retain identical results. For example, V2V3D's average PSNR/SSIM remains 39.05/0.898, and Table 2 retains its 0.413-second runtime and 210.77 million parameters.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10 and their mathematical content are unchanged, including forward projection, PSF reversal, feature alignment, and losses. The common underlying 3D signal and independent view-noise assumptions are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: unsupervised joint denoising and reconstruction, wave-optics-based feature alignment, an LFM dataset, and claimed reconstruction-quality and efficiency advantages.

C2.justification: The explanations of noise removal, detail recovery, and reconstruction artifacts are unchanged. Section 5 retains the same limitations concerning simple volume averaging and dependence on accurate PSFs.

D1.justification: The disclosed architecture, data construction, NVIDIA A100 hardware, loss weights, and access information remain unchanged. Both versions retain the same code/dataset release statement and references to supplementary implementation details.

R1.justification: The same 53 references and related-work discussion are retained, with no added citations or revised positioning against reconstruction and microscopy-denoising methods.

P1.justification: Section 6 changes a funding identifier from 62171255 to 62422110, and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. Research prose, terminology, and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–7 and Tables 1–3 retain their panels, labels, captions, formatting, and placement. Visual inspection confirms no figure redesign, table restructuring, or page-layout revision.

improvement.justification: The funding-number update in Section 6 and routine version metadata do not materially affect the paper's quality. The method, experimental evidence, theoretical content, limitations, reproducibility information, and visual presentation remain unchanged.
